releaseEvidence: The release's own files (linux-release.json, RELEASE-MANIFEST.json, Sigstore-signed SHA256SUMS, blanc-repository.asc) and its approved release notes; chromium/reports/l3-linux.json on chromium/next (build checks 45076009487 and 45076276413, update proof 45103487653, repository lifecycle 45103802669, verify-public 45108455963) and the owner's VM hand checks in chromium/linux/hand-checks-l3.md on chromium/next.

ownerDecisions.status: Pending: the owner approves this copy in its website PR before it merges or deploys (L3 gate item 5 in chromium/reports/l3-linux.json).
decisions: A Linux beta is its own GitHub pre-release, never latest, tagged chromium-beta-linux-<version>, version 158.0.8127.<build>, with .deb and .rpm packages for x64 and arm64 (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-linux-fork-design.md and the L3 plan on chromium/next).

The Download page's Linux tile offers both packages for each architecture and the commands of chromium/linux/manual-repository.md (L3 plan); its update wording says 'offered', never 'installed automatically' (L3 plan decision 5, spec section 3).
Public copy names only the systems a gate ran on, and says KDE and x64 desktops weren't checked by eye (spec sections 1 and 2).

The update wording doesn't promise that the desktop's graphical updater lists Blanc's updates: Ubuntu 26.04's App Center doesn't list them until the repository publishes DEP-11 metadata (chromium/linux/hand-checks-l3.md).
No /dl/* route for Linux in this change: the four packages link straight to the release's assets.

Blanc Beta for Linux
Blanc built directly on Chromium, for Linux.

claims.evidence: Its own package name (blanc-beta), install folder (/opt/bnfy/blanc-beta) and data folder (~/.config/blanc-beta); the release notes say the regular Blanc and its data are left untouched, and the update proof and verify-public legs (45103487653, 45108455963) install it from packages alone.

claims.text: Installing the package adds Blanc’s own signed package repository.
claims.evidence: The package's cron job writes the apt source or dnf repository for https://pkg.blanc.day with Blanc's key (fingerprint 50D3 6197 4F47 7C8C 87E1 17BD 95AE 97AB CACF EE6C); hand check 1 in chromium/linux/hand-checks-l3.md and the repository lifecycle run (45103802669); the dnf repository checks both package and metadata signatures (gpgcheck, repo_gpgcheck).

claims.text: New betas are then offered with your system updates through apt or dnf, and within about two hours of installing one, Blanc shows Restart to update in the Island.
claims.evidence: The update proof (45103487653) moved 905 to 906 through apt and dnf on every leg; hand check 4 (chromium/linux/hand-checks-l3.md) showed Restart to update in the Island and relaunched into 906. Chromium polls the installed version every 2 hours (installed_version_poller.cc), so 'within about two hours', matching the approved release notes. 'Offered', never 'installed automatically' (unattended upgrades skip third-party repositories unless allowed); it doesn't claim a graphical updater lists it (Ubuntu 26.04's App Center doesn't yet).

claims.text: Install and update checks ran on Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 12 and Fedora 45, on x64 and arm64.
claims.evidence: The update proof (45103487653), repository lifecycle (45103802669) and verify-public (45108455963) legs x64-ubuntu, x64-debian, x64-fedora, arm64-ubuntu, arm64-debian and arm64-fedora (chromium/reports/l3-linux.json); the approved release notes' 'Tested on'.

claims.text: Ubuntu 26.04 with GNOME on Wayland was also checked by hand on arm64.
claims.evidence: The owner's Ubuntu 26.04 ARM64 VM, GNOME on Wayland (chromium/linux/hand-checks-l3.md, November 22, 2026).

claims.text: KDE and x64 desktops haven’t been checked by hand.
claims.evidence: The only hand checks ran in the owner's arm64 GNOME VM; the spec requires public copy to say KDE and x64 desktops are unchecked by eye (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-linux-fork-design.md, section 2).

claims.text: It doesn’t make itself your default browser, but where none is chosen yet, as on a fresh Ubuntu 26.04, links from other apps may open in it until you pick one in Settings.
claims.evidence: Hand check 7 (chromium/linux/hand-checks-l3.md): nothing was written to mimeapps.list, and gio names blanc-beta.desktop for https because it is the only registered browser; the approved release notes say the same.

claims.text: Set up the repository yourself
To install the package without adding the repository, run this before installing it.
claims.evidence: chromium/linux/manual-repository.md, 'Turn off automatic repository setup'; the repository lifecycle run (45103802669) checks that with the opt-out set the cron never writes a source.

claims.text: To add the repository by hand instead, first download Blanc’s key and check it.
claims.evidence: chromium/linux/manual-repository.md, 'Download and verify the key': the command refuses a key whose fingerprint isn't 50D361974F477C8C87E117BD95AE97ABCACFEE6C.

claims.text: Then, on Debian and Ubuntu, add the source and install with sudo apt-get install blanc-beta.
claims.evidence: chromium/linux/manual-repository.md, 'Debian and Ubuntu'; the repository lifecycle run (45103802669) runs the manual setup on a fresh system.

claims.text: On Fedora, add the source and install with sudo dnf install blanc-beta.
claims.evidence: chromium/linux/manual-repository.md, 'Fedora'; the repository lifecycle run (45103802669) runs the manual setup on a fresh system.

claims.text: Full guide, including how to turn the repository off
claims.evidence: chromium/linux/manual-repository.md on chromium/next, whose 'Disable an existing source' section removes the source and key files.

claims.text: Not in this beta yet
Protected video, such as Netflix or Spotify.
claims.evidence: The Linux beta is built without Widevine (enable_widevine = false in chromium/linux/args/beta-x64.gn and beta-arm64.gn on chromium/next); the approved release notes say protected video doesn't play.

claims.evidence: The approved release notes say Sync is included but still being checked against the live service, so don't rely on it yet.
